summary: Richard von Garbe specialized in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied under Hermann Grassmann, Rudolf von Roth, and Bhagavata Acharya, earning his PhD from Tübingen and Habilitation at Königsberg. He taught at Königsberg (1878–1895) and Tübingen (1895–1927).

Richard von Glahn is a scholar of Sinology, history, and archaeology. He held a professorship at the University of California, Los Angeles around 1987 and was a visiting fellow at the University of Tokyo from 1988 to 1989.

Rico Sennrich is a computational linguist who earned his PhD from the University of Zurich in 2013, having held a post there around 2010. He subsequently served as a lecturer at the University of Edinburgh from 2015 to 2022.
Rigdzin Shikpo was a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who studied under Chögyam Trungpa and Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche.
Rigzin Lhundup is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who held a professorship at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara, attested in 1959 and 1987.

Riika J. Virtanen is a Tibetologist who completed doctoral studies at the University of Helsinki, supervised by Asko Parpola, Klaus Karttunen, and Hannu Riikonen, and also studied under Sangye Tandar Naga.
Rik Pinxten is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who earned two doctorates at Ghent University in 1975. He later served as a professor at Ghent University from 1981 to 2012.
Rikizan Ishikawa was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University and later served there as Professor of Buddhist Studies until 1997.

Ringu Tulku is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, Namgyal Institute, and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University under teachers including Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, the 16th Karmapa, and Tubten Tsondru.

Rinzin Thargyal is a scholar of Tibetology, history, and archaeology. He earned a Magister degree from the University of Oslo by 1985, studying under supervisors Fredrik Barth and Arne Martin Klausen.
Rita Gupta is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who studied under David Friedman and held a post at North-Eastern Hill University.

Rita Langer is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. She studied at the University of Hamburg (PhD 2004), SOAS, and the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies. She held posts at the University of Bristol.

Rita M. Gross was a religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar who completed her dissertation at the University of Chicago. She served as Professor of Philosophy and Religious Studies at the University of Wisconsin–Eau Claire (~1973–1998).

Rizong Sras Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He trained at Drepung Loseling Monastery (1950–1959) and served as Abbot of Gyume Tantric College (attested 1980), Drepung Loseling (1984), Samstanling Monastery, and 102nd Ganden Thripa (2009–2016).

Ričardas Mironas was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Vytautas Magnus University and the Sorbonne. He held posts as Assistant Instructor (1944) and Associate Professor (1946) at Vytautas Magnus University, and became Professor at Vilnius University in 1950.

Rob Linrothe is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and art history who completed his PhD at the University of Chicago (~1986–1992). He held academic posts at Skidmore College (1992–2009) and Northwestern University (2010–2022).

Rob Nairn was a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned degrees from the University of Zimbabwe, King's College London, and Edinburgh. He served as senior lecturer at the University of Zimbabwe (~1967–1976) and professor at the University of Cape Town (~1977–1980).

Robert A. F. Thurman worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, studying under Geshe Wangyal, Vasudev Vishwanath Gokhale, Gelek Rimpoche, and the 14th Dalai Lama. He held posts at Amherst College (1973–1988) and as Director at Columbia University (1988–2019).

Robert A. Hall, Jr. was a linguist who earned degrees from Princeton, Sapienza University of Rome, and Chicago, where he studied under Leonard Bloomfield and Carl Darling Buck. He served as Professor of Linguistics at Cornell University from 1946 to 1976.
Robert Alan Goodding is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned his PhD from the University of Texas at Austin by 2002 under the supervision of Patrick Olivelle.
